extracted.intended_audience: State Departments of Transportation (State DOTs), Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), FHWA staff, and other stakeholders involved in transportation performance management and GHG reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how State DOTs and MPOs must calculate, set targets for, report, and document progress for the greenhouse gas (GHG) performance measure on the National Highway System (NHS) under 23 CFR part 490.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target setting frequency and initial target date
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs and MPOs will establish or adjust targets every two years beginning in 2024. Targets will first be established for this measure by State DOTs and reported to FHWA in a State Initial GHG Report, no later than February 1, 2024. Because initial targets will be established so close to the mid-point, 2-year targets will not be required initially; 4-year targets are required and must be established no later than February 1, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 23 CFR 490.105(e)(1)(ii), 490.105(e)(4)(iii), and 490.107(d). The information provided in the 2024 State Initial GHG Report will be considered the 2024 Mid Performance Period Progress Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Initial GHG Report content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Initial GHG Report must include the 4-year target, the basis for the target, the baseline data (the reference year for this performance period only), the relationship with other performance expectations, the data points used to calculate the GHG metric (described in 23 CFR 490.511(c)), and the value calculated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 23 CFR 490.107(d)(2). These requirements are similar to the Baseline Performance Period Report and are the basis for initial target establishment and future reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: State reporting cycle (biennial/October 1 alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOT reporting is biennial and will follow an October 1st cycle beginning in 2026 to align with other measure reporting requirements; the biennial reporting cycle established in 23 CFR 490.107(b) remains in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 150(e) of Title 23 U.S.C. requires State DOTs to report biennially. The two-year reporting aligns with other TPM measures and minimizes incremental burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPO reporting frequency and process
rubrics_metrics.description: MPOs are required to report on performance within their metropolitan transportation plan (MTP) (developed every 4 or 5 years) and in system performance reports; FHWA will not require an additional biennial report outside of the MTP process for MPOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 23 CFR 450.324(d) and 23 CFR 490.107(c). FHWA retained requirement for MPOs to report progress toward their GHG target in the system performance report in the metropolitan plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPO report content and metric reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: MPOs must report the metrics used to calculate the GHG measure and the metric calculation method(s); report baseline performance and progress toward targets; report calculation of annual tailpipe CO2 emissions for the NHS for the period between the reference year and the first system performance report that includes the GHG measure; and subsequently cover periods between reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA removed the proposed requirement for MPOs to report tailpipe CO2 emissions on all roads. MPOs using metric calculation methods not specified in 23 CFR 490.511(d) must include information demonstrating the method(s) has valid and useful results for measuring transportation-related CO2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for MPO methods not specified in regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an MPO uses a metric calculation method not specified in 23 CFR 490.511(d), the MPO must demonstrate in the system performance report that the method is valid and useful for measuring transportation-related CO2 emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added requirement to 23 CFR 490.107(c)(2)(ii). This replaces the prior requirement for mutual agreement with the State DOT and aims to ensure accountability without imposing concurrence burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability / transparency of reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA will publish State DOT biennial reports and FHWA's significant progress determinations on its publicly available TPM Dashboards, and the GHG measure will be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State performance dashboards and reports available at https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/tpm/reporting/state/. External reporting on U.S. DOT funds spent is outside the scope of this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant progress determination criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA will determine that a State DOT has made significant progress toward a 2-year or 4-year applicable GHG target if (1) the actual performance level is better than the baseline performance, or (2) the actual performance level is equal to or better than the established target, as defined in 23 CFR 490.109(e)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA declined to narrow the definition and retained consistency with existing significant progress criteria used for other NHPP and NHFP measures (see 23 CFR 490.105(c)(1)-(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of significant progress assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA will not assess significant progress for the GHG measure after the 2024 Mid Performance Period Progress Report; the first significant progress assessment for the GHG measure will occur after the 2026 Full Performance Period Progress Report (due October 1, 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conducting the significant progress determination after the 2026 report, the performance for the reference year shall be used as the baseline performance (see 23 CFR 490.105(e)(10)(i)(C)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation required when significant progress not achieved
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State DOT does not make significant progress, FHWA expects the State DOT to provide data-supported explanations for not achieving significant progress and a plan to achieve progress in the future; the documentation requirements in 23 CFR 490.109(f)(1)(v) represent the minimum federally required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA does not intend to use significant progress determination punitively and will not add additional consequences that create undue burden; States may provide additional detail voluntarily in biennial reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roadway applicability (NHS only)
rubrics_metrics.description: The GHG measure applies to performance on the National Highway System (Interstate System and non-Interstate NHS) only; FHWA does not have statutory authority under 23 U.S.C. 150(c)(3)(A)(ii)-(V) to require measures for all public roads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although NHS captures only a portion of roadways, State DOTs and MPOs may choose to implement additional measures that apply to all roads to suit local policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference year selection
rubrics_metrics.description: 2022 is established as the reference year for the GHG measure (not 2021) because 2021 was affected by the COVID-19 pandemic and 2022 more closely reflects pre-pandemic travel activity and is the most recent year with finalized VMT estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA cites Traffic Volume Trends showing 2022 VMT nearly rebounded to 2019 levels; finalized VMT estimates for 2022 expected by November 30, 2023 for use in calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / scope of GHG emissions for the measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Although GHGs generally include CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, FHWA concluded that approximately 97% of on-road GHG emissions (on a 100-year GWP-weighted basis) are CO2; the measure will focus on tailpipe CO2 emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including non-CO2 gases in this tailpipe-focused measure would not yield significant benefits; any expansion beyond tailpipe CO2 would require notice-and-comment rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform CO2 emissions factors for States
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA will publish uniform CO2 emissions factors for each fuel type to be used by all States in calculating the State DOT metric for the GHG measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform factors ensure consistency and comparability. FHWA will consider EPA accounting practices for biofuels and will publish these factors on its website by August 15 of each biennial reporting year.

rubrics_metrics.name: VMT and data availability for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs may use their best available VMT data that represents the prior calendar year when reporting performance and metric information in biennial reports; because data used by State DOTs may not be known to FHWA, States must provide the values used and describe the data source(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 23 CFR 490.509(h) was revised to allow use of best available VMT; related reporting requirement revisions in 490.107(b) and 490.511(f)(2) require States to document VMT values and data sources. FHWA specified HPMS-based dates for baseline/reference data acceptance (HPMS as of Nov 30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fuel sales data source and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA's Fuels & FASH database (Monthly Motor Fuel Report) will serve as the source of fuel use data; States submit preliminary monthly fuel volumes for gasoline and special fuel (diesel) due to FHWA 90 days after month-end, and final estimated fuel volumes for a given year will be available by August 15 of the following year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States' preliminary estimates are publicly available and used to support early reporting; FHWA adjusts final estimates for updated monthly state submissions and non-highway fuel use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment for non-highway fuel use
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA uses modeling to estimate the portion of fuel sales consumed off-highway and adjusts gasoline volume data submitted by States to identify on-highway volumes; States are instructed not to report non-highway use of special fuels (red dyed diesel, kerosene).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These adjustments aim to isolate on-highway fuel use for CO2 calculation, acknowledging cross-border fuel purchases and other sources of misalignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: State DOT metric calculation method (fuel-based approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: State CO2 estimates are calculated by multiplying gallons of fuel taxed by each State by the CO2 emissions factor for each fuel type (using FHWA uniform factors), with States calculating CO2 for all roads and then estimating the NHS share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA retained the fuel-sales-based approach because it provides comparability and better captures total fuel consumption (including induced demand) versus model-based approaches; it assumes similar GHG emission rates per VMT for NHS and non-NHS facilities as a simplifying assumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPO metric calculation flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: MPOs are permitted flexibility to use a range of approaches to calculate the GHG metric (including calculating NHS emissions directly); FHWA preserved this flexibility because technical capabilities vary across MPOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA removed the requirement for MPOs to report tailpipe CO2 for all roads. MPOs that choose methods not enumerated in 490.511(d) must demonstrate validity/usefulness; FHWA encourages coordination with State DOTs but no longer requires mutual agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual agreement on MPO method not required (coordination encouraged)
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA will not require that an MPO's metric calculation method be mutually agreed upon by the State DOT and MPO; MPOs are encouraged to coordinate with State DOTs on data to the maximum extent practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of mutual agreement, if the method is not specified in 490.511(d) the MPO must demonstrate validity/usefulness in the system performance report (see 490.107(c)(2)(ii)). FHWA cites 23 CFR part 450 collaboration/coordination expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PBPP alignment requirement for MPO plans and TIPs
rubrics_metrics.description: An MPO's MTP and TIP must meet the Performance-Based Planning and Programming (PBPP) requirements of the planning rule for the GHG performance measure by no later than 2 years after the effective date of this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with 23 CFR 450.226 and 23 CFR 450.340.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data acceptance dates for significant progress determination
rubrics_metrics.description: For significant progress determinations, baseline performance will be based on HPMS data as of November 30 of the baseline report year and the reference year will be based on HPMS data as of November 30, 2023; data used must be accepted by FHWA by dates specified in 490.109(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specifications result from revisions to 23 CFR 490.509(h) and related reporting rules to ensure State DOTs can use their most accurate VMT data for estimating NHS share of on-road tailpipe CO2 emissions.
